title: Wisconsin ADU law: statewide estimates

outcome.short: Second-home permits at issuance on lots that already have a single-family home. Not completed homes. Results are for areas, never individual lots.
outcome.long: The outcome is permits for a second home on a lot that already has a single-family home: accessory dwelling units (ADUs) plus single-family-to-duplex conversions (AQ-032), counted when the permit is issued. They are not completed homes and not net new housing. Every result is for an area (the state, a county, or a city, village or town); the tool never predicts which lot will build.
outcome.rate_units: permits per 1,000 single-family homes per year

terms.scenarios: Lower, central and Strong adoption: how Wisconsin could respond, based on how much the statewide-law states differ from one another. Not statistical confidence intervals.
terms.sensitivity_case: Changes one assumption and reruns the model. Together the cases are the sensitivity analysis.
terms.robustness_check: Tests a methodological alternative by predicting held-out states.
terms.baseline: What the model expects under current law, with no statewide ADU law.
terms.additional: Permits the statewide law adds on top of the baseline.
terms.never_subtracts: A statewide law never subtracts permits. Where a place already permits more than the law's expected rate for it, for example because its own rules go further than the benchmark (Madison's two-unit ADU buildings, or San Diego's bonus ADU programme in California), the law adds nothing there and the place keeps its current-law permits: each place's addition is floored at zero, never negative.

pilot_intro.title: What is a pilot page?
pilot_intro.text: This pilot page allows you to see a few of the steps we took on the way to building the statewide model. The work started here: real permit records from Wisconsin places, above all these three (Madison, Pleasant Prairie and Sun Prairie), measure how many second homes places permit today under their current rules, and Madison's level sets the minimum rate every Wisconsin place reaches with the law.
pilot_intro.how: The statewide estimate itself is built top-down, from how eight other states responded to their statewide ADU laws. Each pilot page then shows how that statewide result is shared out to one real place, and acts as a spot check on it. The pilots are not a separate, bottom-up model: their figures are already inside the Wisconsin total and are never added to it.

status_pills.observed: Observed: counted in a published source or permit record.
status_pills.calculated: Calculated: computed by the model from observed inputs and stated rules.
status_pills.assumed: Assumed: a judgment or default where no local data exist.

limitations: Permits, not completed homes; some permitted ADUs are never built.
No Midwest state has data after a statewide law; Wisconsin's response is transferred from eight other states.
69% of single-family homes are in places whose ADU rules are not coded; they are treated as restricted.
Town and village figures are rough shares of the statewide result, not local forecasts.
Results are associations observed after other states' laws, not proven causal effects.
Pilot pages are examples; they are never added up into a Wisconsin total.
